thread:
sara (infra): Heads up — seeing a recurring hotspot in eu-west-2 racks 11-13 for the last 3 hours. GPU temp + tail latency spike correlated with cross-region allocations that prefer those racks. Looks like routing is biasing towards them because of recent prefill. :frowning_face:

infra-bot: [ALERT] 2025-09-04T13:10Z eu-west-2 rack-11 GPU temp above 85C, avg token latency +42ms, alloc churn +18% (link: https://telemetry/redwood/alerts/1751592653)

ajay: Ugh. Is this impacting Dedicated pools or just shared slices?

sara (infra): Mostly shared slices but we saw a hitch where a fractional dedicated carveout got a spillback during a warmup, caused noisy neighbor-like interference on NPU lanes. No full evictions yet.

mike: Do we have a quick mitigation? Can we bias routing away preemptively rather than wait for thermal OOMs?

dani: We can add a short-term bias to the allocator that decays after 60s. That should steer new allocs off hot racks without touching pinned dedicated nodes. Needs a safety rule for dedicated: never shift if tenant has reserved capacity tag.

ajay: +1 on reserved-tag safety. Also want to avoid oscillation — need smoothing + cooldown.

mike: Proposed policy snippet (testing):
```yaml
routing_policy: hotspot_bias_v1
parameters:
  lookback: 30s
  weight_decay: 0.65
  cooldown: 90s
  max_shift_pct: 15 # pct of new allocs redirected per window
  respect_reserved: true
```

lina: Cost note — if we bias away to other regions we'll pay egress/latency penalties for some customers. We should scope it to same-region AZs first.

sara (infra): Agreed. Plan: 1) Apply a same-region AZ bias (canary on eu-west-2a only) 2) Respect reserved/dedicated tags 3) Monitor per-tenant latency and cost delta for 30m 4) Rollback if any reserve-tagged allocs see >5% error increase.

ajay: How do we surface the cost delta in the console? Can we tag rollout with a cost-ticker?

dani: We can annotate the rollout with telemetry labels and have Optimize emit a delta per tenant. Quick command: `rkctl routes apply --policy hotspot-bias-v1 --scope eu-west-2a --canary 5`

infra-bot: [INFO] Started canary hotspot-bias-v1 in eu-west-2a at 2025-09-04T13:20Z (5% traffic). Metric hooks: gpu_temp, token_latency_p95, egress_bytes, reserved_violations.

mike: I'll watch telemetry and keep an eye on dedicated p95. If we see reserved_violations pop up, I'll flip the policy off immediately.

lina: Also flag Finance — if we push cross-AZ traffic costs > $X/hr we need approval. I'll open a quick ticket.

ajay: One more ask — add a small probe that checks NVLink congestion heuristics. If NVLink saturation > 70% in target rack, block shift. That avoids routing into IO-congested racks.

sara (infra): Good call. Dani, can you add NVLink check to the gating rules?

dani: Yep. I'll add `nvlink_util_pct < 70` as a gating rule and a 15s re-eval window. Pushing branch `hotspot-bias-nvlink` now.

sara (infra): Perfect. Action items: dani - push gate + canary config; mike - monitor and rollback guard; lina - finance ticket; ajay - add probe to scheduler test harness. We'll reconvene in 30m. :eyes:

mike: on it. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: [METRICS SNAPSHOT] pre-canary: rack-11 gpu_temp=86C p95=310ms; rack-12 gpu_temp=83C p95=295ms; reserved_violations=0

sara (infra): thanks folks — if canary looks stable we'll roll to 25% then 50% next hour. Keep short replies here for quick coordination.

ajay: noted.

lina: ticket opened: FIN-3281 (linked).

dani: branch pushed and canary applied. `rkctl routes apply` returned success.

mike: seeing initial drop in new allocs landing on racks 11-13. temp trending down ~3C after 6m.

sara (infra): nice. leaving this thread pinned for the next hour.

ajay: +1
